issue.title: uv.lock on main fails to parse: duplicate package pyvespa==1.2.9
issue.body:
### Description

`uv lock --check` (and `uv sync --frozen`) fails on a clean `main`:

```
error: Failed to parse `uv.lock`
  cause: Found duplicate package `pyvespa==1.2.9 @ registry+https://pypi.org/simple`
```

Reproduced with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1 and 0.13.3 on `main` at `0a4b5d8e49` and
current `6aee277d4a` (macOS arm64). The `uv.lock` blob is
`eb0774d98a4571fd1a0359d8536d4b13aa41422b` (sha256
`cf8f72edaff55fa77a1ca03445032adf7e5b346f7c93154592408e5c2ac64014`); I copied
that exact blob from `git show upstream/main:uv.lock` into an isolated temp
directory and reproduced the parse failure with all three versions, so this is
not caused by the workspace or a local environment. `uv sync --frozen --project
airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` fails with the same error.

### Cause

`uv.lock` is internally inconsistent after #73822:

- the two `pyvespa` package blocks were bumped from 1.2.7/1.2.9 to 1.2.9/1.2.9,
  so they are now identical except for `resolution-markers`, and uv reports the
  duplicate package;
- the resolved dependency graph for `apache-airflow-providers-vespa` still points
  at `pyvespa==1.2.7` for `python_version < '3.14'`, although no 1.2.7 package
  block exists anymore. After merging the duplicate blocks, uv then fails with
  `found dependency pyvespa==1.2.7 with no locked package`.

The provider still declares a split constraint:

```toml
# providers/vespa/pyproject.toml
"pyvespa>=1.2.9; python_version >= '3.14'",
"pyvespa>=1.1.2; python_version < '3.14'",
```

That constraint is not the problem: `pyvespa` 1.2.9 supports Python
`>=3.10,<3.16`, so both marker branches can resolve to 1.2.9. A fresh
`uv lock` with the same constraints produces a single 1.2.9 entry, and
replaying the 1.2.7→1.2.9 upgrade with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1, 0.13.2 and 0.13.3
also dedupes correctly. This looks like a one-off inconsistent lock produced by
#73822 rather than a general resolver bug.

### Impact

Every `uv sync --frozen` on current `main` fails, so:

- prek hooks such as `mypy-*`, provider validation and `Update uv.lock` fail;
- CI jobs that sync the workspace fail (e.g. Airflow CTL tests 3.11–3.14,
  Scripts tests and Shared distributions tests on `0a4b5d8e49`);
- the merge ref for PR #75193 fails in Airflow CTL tests, Shared distributions
  tests and the CI image build with the same parse error;
- contributors cannot rebase/push branches onto current `main` without
  `--no-verify`.

### Suggested fix

#### Preferred minimal fix: partially revert the offending `pyvespa` hunk

For `pyvespa`, `#73822` changed only the `<3.14` package block: the version went
from 1.2.7 to 1.2.9, together with the `sdist` and wheel URLs/hashes. The
`apache-airflow-providers-vespa` dependency for `<3.14` was left pointing at
`pyvespa==1.2.7`, which is why the lock is inconsistent.

Restoring just that block to the parent (`0a4b5d8e49^`) content fixes the lock
without touching any other package:

- Python `<3.14`: `pyvespa==1.2.7` (allowed by the provider's `>=1.1.2`
  constraint)
- Python `>=3.14`: `pyvespa==1.2.9`
- `providers/vespa/pyproject.toml` is unchanged

The resulting diff is **3 insertions / 3 deletions**. `uv lock --check` passes
with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1 and 0.13.3; `uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core
--group mypy --dry-run` passes; and running `uv lock` again makes no changes.
This is a targeted revert of the offending part of `#73822`, not a hand-invented
version. It does keep `pyvespa` at 1.2.7 for `<3.14`.

#### Alternative: regenerate the lock

If the intent is to keep `pyvespa` 1.2.9 for `<3.14` as well, regenerate
`uv.lock` with uv rather than hand-edit it. A fresh `uv lock` on current `main`
succeeds and produces a single `pyvespa==1.2.9` package block with no resolution
markers. `uv lock --check` passes with uv 0.13.1 and 0.13.3, and
`uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` succeeds.

The generated lock differs from the current broken one by 803 changed lines
(441 insertions / 362 deletions). It contains 990 packages, with 40 package
names changed and one added (`google-cloud-sql`); examples of unrelated updates
include `pydantic-ai-slim` 2.56.0→2.57.0, `snowflake-connector-python`
5.0.0rc5→5.0.0 and several `google-cloud-*` packages. Starting from the last
valid lock (`0a4b5d8e49^`) and running `uv lock --upgrade` produces a
byte-identical lock, so this is the resolver's current canonical result, not an
artifact of deleting the file.

#### Emergency recovery: hand-repair the duplicate blocks

If a targeted partial revert or a full regeneration is not possible, the lock
can be hand-repaired as an emergency recovery:

1. merge the two `pyvespa==1.2.9` `[[package]]` blocks into one, dropping the
   redundant `resolution-markers`;
2. change the `< 3.14` resolved dependency of
   `apache-airflow-providers-vespa` from `pyvespa==1.2.7` to `pyvespa==1.2.9`.

With these two edits, `uv lock --check` passes with uv 0.13.1 and 0.13.3,
`uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` passes, and the
lock diff is 1 insertion / 47 deletions. This is a recovery for the unparseable
file, not the normal generated workflow, and should only be used if the larger
regeneration diff is not acceptable.

The provider constraint does not need to change in any case.

### Environment

- uv 0.13.3 (also reproduced with 0.12.18 and 0.13.1)
- macOS arm64; repo venv CPython 3.12.15, isolated probe used CPython 3.14.7
  selected by uv
- `uv.lock` revision 5, `requires-python >=3.11`

Related: #73822, #75062
